scope.content_boundary: Review of statements, hypotheses, counterexamples, ownership and source scope; not completed theorem proofs.

closures.evidence: The statement and UniformDeterminant supporting construction use compactness of the trace-norm image, pointwise continuity and a finite subcover. Holomorphy is owned via normal convergence of the exterior-power series. No quantitative bound is attributed to RandomMatrices §8.3.

Every index-zero Fredholm chart obtains the local section det S from an equal-rank finite-dimensional stabilization, with d log(det S)=Tr(S⁻¹dS) and frame corrections. An infinite-dimensional integrable-kernel trace formula additionally requires a trace-norm holomorphic realization and τ=u det(I−K), including d log u. JMU/Hamiltonian comparisons retain the generic unramified nonresonant scope. The e^s I diagnostic is valid. Remaining Check4 terminology is recorded separately as AR2-02.

PicardObstructions explicitly restricts absolute H² vanishing to affine square-zero test bases with arbitrary quasi-coherent ideal. It distinguishes relative R^q p_* vanishing from absolute cohomology, uses affine-base Leray, and treats general test bases through descent. Restriction isomorphisms are retained in the H¹ torsor claim.

AnalyticCarrier names the nilpotent-preserving analytic foundational prefix of M1.2, owns local charts/gluing/base change, and excludes moduli/RH/Painlevé theorem input. The target-level M1.2 dependency is present and does not introduce an application-to-general dependency.
The weighted moment/tail reference is target:A1.4 in the English statement, Japanese statement and structured plan.

Additional-hypothesis curve/observer theorems are stated as proof obligations; optional wording and parent-file/consolidation/byte-provenance prose are removed from the normative manuscript. The Japanese temporal qualifiers identified in R1 are removed.

Both languages fix external parameters at α₀ and extend the nodal curve along the time base {α₀}×U. Extension in external-parameter directions requires a separately established nodal-curve locus. This agrees with ST04 Proposition 2.1(1)(a), rather than enlarging its conclusion to the full parameter space.

positive_checks: All six R1 analytic-review findings are substantively corrected in English, Japanese and the structured plan; the P7.3 source-scope clarification is present in both languages.

The 23 new Japanese hypotheses for A1.1–A1.6 and C1.1–C1.2 preserve the English assumptions, quantifiers and exclusions. P7–P11 hypothesis pairs have no new mathematical translation mismatch; the placement defect is separate.

The infinite-dimensional family T_s=e^s I is Fredholm but has a non-trace-class logarithmic derivative I ds; the finite-dimensional stabilization construction handles it without asserting an unavailable infinite-dimensional trace.

The generic complete flat connection q′=q/(2t) on ℂ××ℂ gives √t on the universal cover, with nontrivial deck action. Admissibility alone does not establish scalar descent. The added diagnostic correctly distinguishes these assertions.
A1.6 now uses compact-image continuity for compact-uniform determinant convergence, with owned normal-series estimates for holomorphy; it does not rely on an unstated supplier inequality.

The affine-local Picard argument retains arbitrary quasi-coherent square-zero ideals and nonreduced bases. The invalid inference from relative dimension to global H² vanishing over nonaffine bases has been removed.
C1.2 consumes shared analytic carriers without importing connection-moduli conclusions; its declared general dependency closure remains free of Part P/G application targets.

The P10.3 explicit sector bounds, sector angles, branch conventions, weighted arc orders and calibration phase remain unchanged from the reviewed correct specification. Those owned parametrix estimates are still proof obligations, not assumed completed results.

No additional false mathematical assertion or invalid counterexample was detected in the assigned reviewed passages. Geometry-specific fixed-dimension qualification is being handled by the independent geometry reviewer.
